HGV training

Category C, Category C+E and Driver CPC from one base. This page compares the routes. It does not confirm eligibility, a price or a course length.

Licence comparison

Three routes. Each has its own page, so this overview stays a comparison rather than a second copy of the course detail.

RouteWhat it coversUsual starting point
Category CRigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes.Usually a category B car licence, then the medical and theory steps for a lorry test.
Category C+EArticulated lorries and drawbar combinations.Category C is the usual entitlement held before this training.
Driver CPCA professional qualification for lorry and bus drivers. Not a vehicle category.Depends on whether the driver needs initial or periodic CPC.

Which licence is right for me?

General guidance only. The provider checks the licence you hold when you enquire.

  • Category CThe usual route onto a rigid lorry when you hold a car licence and want to drive goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes.
  • Category C+EThe trailer entitlement, for articulated lorries and drawbar outfits, once Category C is held.
  • Driver CPCThe professional qualification that sits alongside the licence for many paid driving jobs. It does not replace Category C or C+E.
Ask which licence fits

Typical training journey

The same sequence a driver can expect to talk through. No timetable is attached.

  1. Say what you want to drive

    Category C, Category C+E or Driver CPC. If you are not sure, say so and the provider can talk it through.

  2. Check what you already hold

    The provider looks at your current licence and explains any medical, theory or CPC steps that sit alongside the practical training. This site does not confirm eligibility.

  3. Train from the local base

    Practical sessions are arranged from one training location. This demonstration does not publish a timetable.

  4. Prepare for the next step

    That may be a practical test or periodic CPC hours. How booking works is explained when you enquire. No result is claimed here.

What training includes

Each course page sets out the practical work. In short, the core offer is:

  • Category CPractical training for rigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, for drivers moving up from a car licence.
  • Category C+ETrailer training for drivers who already hold Category C and need the articulated or drawbar entitlement.
  • Driver CPCPeriodic training for professional drivers. This demonstration does not list a course code, a date or an approval number.

Questions

What is the difference between Category C and Category C+E?

Category C is the rigid lorry entitlement. Category C+E adds a trailer, for articulated lorries and drawbar outfits. C+E training normally follows Category C.

Is Driver CPC the same as an HGV licence?

No. Category C and Category C+E are vehicle entitlements. Driver CPC is a professional qualification for drivers who need a Driver Qualification Card.

Can this page tell me if I am eligible?

No. It is general guidance. The provider checks the licence you hold when you enquire. Nothing here confirms that a particular person qualifies.

Why is there no price list?

Because a fee has not been supplied for this demonstration, and one should not be invented. Ask for a quote for the training you need.
